nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a \ge 2$ and $n \ge 1$, the integer $(a-1)n + 1$ divides the binomial coefficient $\binom{an}{n}$. Hence the Fuss–Catalan number $\frac{1}{(a-1)n+1}\binom{an}{n}$ is an integer.
nodes.title: Integrality of the Fuss–Catalan numbers

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k \ge 1$ (the chord arity) and $m$, the Fuss–Catalan number is the natural-number quotient of $\binom{km}{m}$ by $(k-1)m+1$, that is $\lfloor \binom{km}{m} / ((k-1)m+1) \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Fuss–Catalan numbers

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $n$ a natural number. Then $p$ divides the generalized Catalan number $\frac{1}{(p-1)n+1}\binom{pn}{n}$ (an integer) if and only if $n$ is not of the form $\frac{p^k-1}{p-1}$ for any natural number $k$.
nodes.title: Prime divisibility of generalized Catalan numbers

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$, $n$ and $k$, the generalized Fuss–Catalan number $F_m(n, k)$ equals the quotient of $k \binom{mn + k}{n}$ by $mn + k$ in natural-number division, rounded down, with division by $0$ giving $0$.
nodes.title: Formula for the generalized Fuss–Catalan number

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $k$, the generalized Fuss–Catalan number $F_m(1, k)$ equals $k$.
nodes.title: Generalized Fuss–Catalan numbers at $n = 1$
